title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page shows a 'cube' of ringed topoi attached to a scheme X over a base S (the NB says S is suppressed from the notation). It is meant as an organizing scheme for the theory of crystals and de Rham cohomology.

The diagram:
- Top: X_zar maps to X_conn (connections) and to X_P-conn. 'P' most likely means 'puissances divisées' (divided powers, PD); this reading is not certain.
- Middle layer: X_conn → X_strat (stratifications), labelled 'équiv si car 0'. There is also a dashed arrow X_P-conn → X_strat.
- Vertical arrows: X_conn → X_cris and X_P-conn → X_P-cris, each labelled 'équiv si X/S lisse'. Also X_strat → X_inf (infinitesimal topos).
- Lower layer: dashed X_cris → X_P-cris, solid X_cris → X_inf, dashed X_P-cris → X_inf.
- Bottom: X_cris, X_inf and X_P-cris all map to X_zar.
- The brace says these are morphisms of ringed topoi. The dashed arrows are defined only if X is torsion over Z.
- Left margin: 'détermination des points de ces topos ?'.

In modern terms, Grothendieck wants every category of 'coefficients' to be the module category of a ringed topos:
- modules with integrable connection;
- modules with integrable PD-connection;
- stratifications (modules over the full ring of differential operators);
- crystals on the infinitesimal site;
- crystals on a crystalline site without and with divided powers.
The arrows are the comparison functors. 'Equivalent in char 0' is the classical fact that integrable connections are the same as stratifications (for smooth X). 'Equivalent if smooth' is the comparison of connections with crystals.

The topoi with no natural site description (X_conn, X_P-conn, X_strat) are particularly interesting. Today one would describe them via the formal groupoid / Lie algebroid of X/S, or via de Rham-type stacks.

The text then makes three points.
1. Arrows towards X_zar (projections u: X_cris → X_zar etc.) give Zariski localization isomorphisms and Leray spectral sequences relating crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology to Zariski cohomology. This is how one obtains crystalline cohomology ≅ de Rham cohomology.
2. Arrows from X_zar (the inclusion i) behave like a closed immersion of ringed topoi. On the big topos there is an exact sequence 0 → J → O_X → O_{X_0} → 0, and Mod(X_zar) ≃ Mod(O_{X_0}).
3. For an invertible sheaf L on X_zar, one defines a Chern class c'(L) in H^2(X_cris) and in H^2(X_P-cris), compatible when X is torsion. It is the coboundary of the class of L under the exact sequence 1 → 1+J → O_X^* → O_{X_0}^* → 1. This gives a class in H^2(X_cris, 1+J), which in the PD case can be mapped via log to J and then to O. On X_cris its vanishing is necessary and sufficient for L to come from an invertible crystal, i.e. in the smooth relative case for L to admit an integrable connection.
This is the crystalline Chern class as an obstruction class.
errors: 'X_conn → X_cris équiv si X/S lisse': if X_cris is the PD crystalline site, then in characteristic p crystals correspond only to modules with quasi-nilpotent integrable connection, so the equivalence needs a nilpotence restriction. If X_cris is a non-PD variant, the equivalence with integrable connections in char p is doubtful. The statement is imprecise as written.
'équiv si car 0' for connections vs stratifications also needs X/S smooth (or at least formally smooth).

The claim Mod(X_zar) ≃ Mod(O_{X_0}) on the crystalline/infinitesimal topos is delicate. i_* is fully faithful, but identifying all O_{X_0}-modules on the big site with Zariski modules requires care. It is not literally a closed subtopos in the topos-theoretic sense.

The obstruction statement uses the multiplicative class in H^2(X_cris, 1+J). The additive Chern class in H^2(X_cris, O) is obtained only after a logarithm, which needs divided powers. The 'c'' notation conflates the two.

ideas.what: Systematic cube of ringed topoi (Zariski, connections, PD-connections, stratifications, crystalline, PD-crystalline, infinitesimal) with comparison morphisms
ideas.modern_name: comparison of coefficient theories: D-modules / stratifications / crystals; infinitesimal vs crystalline topos
ideas.where_published: Partially in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); the topos-theoretic packaging of connections as ringed topoi is unsure

ideas.what: Treating modules with integrable connection (and PD-connection, stratification) as modules over a ringed topos X_conn, X_strat
ideas.modern_name: classifying topos of a formal groupoid / Lie algebroid; de Rham stack X_dR
ideas.usually_credited_to: Simpson (de Rham stack, 1990s); Berthelot (PD differential operators of level 0)

ideas.what: Projection X_cris → X_zar gives localization isomorphisms and Leray spectral sequences
X_zar → X_cris as a closed immersion of ringed topoi with ideal J
Crystalline Chern class of a line bundle as coboundary; its vanishing is the obstruction to extending L to an invertible crystal (integrable connection)
ideas.modern_name: crystalline first Chern class / obstruction to integrable connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Illusie, 'Classes de Chern en cohomologie cristalline' (1970); Atiyah class

ideas.what: Question of determining the points of these topoi

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for the points of the crystalline, infinitesimal, connection and stratification topoi. As far as I know, a systematic description of the points of these topoi (especially the non-site-defined X_conn, X_strat) is not in the literature.
missed.quote: détermination des points de ces topos ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Points of crystalline/prismatic-type topoi relate to understanding stalks and conservativity in crystalline, prismatic and de Rham stack approaches.

missed.claim: Coefficient categories (integrable connections, PD-connections, stratifications) are envisaged as module categories of genuine ringed topoi, fitting functorially in one cube with the crystalline and infinitesimal topoi. This anticipates the stacky viewpoint (X_dR, crystalline/de Rham stacks) where all coefficient theories are sheaves on a geometric object.
missed.quote: X_conn ... X_strat ... morphismes de topos annelés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close in spirit to Simpson's de Rham stack and recent stacky approaches (Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie); it is a mild early anticipation.

deep.surprise_reason: Most content (crystalline/infinitesimal comparison, closed immersion i, Chern class as obstruction) is now standard via Grothendieck's Crystals notes and Berthelot / Berthelot–Illusie. The mildly notable elements are two. First, connections and stratifications are presented as ringed topoi in a single cube of morphisms. Second, the open question on the points of these topoi.
